newsitem.title: NORWAY: DnB makes bid for BNbank.
newsitem.headline: DnB makes bid for BNbank.

text.p: Norway's largest commercial bank Den norske Bank ASA (DnB) said on Friday it had launched a bid for Bolig og Naeringsbanken (BNbank).
DnB said it had offered a cash payment of 184.50 crowns per share, plus BNbank's 1996 dividend of 10.50 crowns.
"The total value of BNbank is thus stipulated at NOK 1,875 million," DnB said in a statement.
DnB's offer comes three days after Norway's fourth largest bank, Trondheim-based Fokus Bank ASA, proposed a merger with BNbank, a niche institution specialising in mortgage loans.

Fokus proposed an exchange ratio of 3.3 shares in Fokus Bank for each share in BNbank, with 20 percent of the consideration paid in cash. Based on Fokus' closing share price on Monday of 58.50 crowns, the exchange ratio equalled a price on BNbank of 179.85 crowns per share and 10 crowns in dividend, Fokus said in its statement.
Fokus told Reuters after learning of DnB's counterbid that it planned to revise the situation.
DnB currently owns 7.4 percent of BNbank shares, and an additional 0.9 percent held by its insurance subsidiary Vital Forsikring.

"Through the purchase of BNbank, DnB wishes to strengthen Trondheim as a centre of expertise as part of a major effort directed towards customers in the Troendelag region, and at the same time enhance DnB's position in the market for long-term morgage loans to the business sector," DnB's statement said.

At 0936 GMT, DnB's share price was up 0.40 crowns at 27.50 crowns, while BNbank had gained one crown to 194.50 in hefty trade of 66.4 million crowns. At the same time Fokus was down 3.50 crowns at 55.50 crowns in thin volume.
